notes: A resource-procurement op, not a fight: the whole thing is a shopping list handed out by the Quartermaster and handed back to him. Bullet [1] ('Solo mission') is advice, not a step. The ladder is therefore two rungs on ONE NPC, which is right -- consecutive steps on the same NPC are one marker and readiness looks ahead across them. The walkthrough never mentions signing up with, or reporting back to, Emhi Tchaoryo even though he is the op's giver; no step is invented for it and the header's giver is recorded in start. That gap is why walkthrough_incomplete is flagged. Bullet [3]'s list of candidate supplies is DROPPED by the renderer -- the wikitext has 21 ':*' sub-entries under it (Bretzel x33, Meat Mithkabob x6, Tomato Soup x1, Iron Bread x12, Pepper Biscuit x9, Nebimonite Bake x1, Ginger Cookie x33, Black Bread x12, Melon Juice x1, Grape Juice x1, Beaugreen Saute x1, Eel Kabob x1, Salmon Roe x1, Windurst Salad x1, Acorn Cookie x33, Tomato Juice x1, Pamama Tart x1, Icecap Rolanberry x1, Apple Pie x4, and two repeats). It is a list of POSSIBLE requests -- 'different players' get different sets -- so it is not an AND-list and none of it is recorded as items; items_partial carries the fact that the real requirement cannot be expressed. No evidence anywhere: the supplies are ordinary stackable food that a player may hold for any reason, and they are consumed on submission. The bullet gives the Quartermaster by landmark and no grid; BG Wiki's Quartermaster page (fetched from the REST API) puts the Windurst Waters (S) Quartermaster at (F-9), which is recorded in the step note rather than in grid, because the page being read states no grid for this step. Campaign Rank is empty on this page, so no rank gate. gates.repeatable and gates.expansion are left null: the Campaign Header carries no Repeatable and no Expansion field, and an explicit null is the tri-state 'the page did not say' rather than a claim that it does not repeat.

notes: A fixed-location BCNM op, so unlike the supply/escort ops this ladder can carry real places all the way through. Bullet [3] (the 30 minute cap) is not a step and rides in the fight step's note. That is the last rung. The 15 Yagudos are deliberately NOT recorded as mobs: 'Yagudo' is a race, not a mob name, and mobs are matched live against the entity list by folded name, so it would either match nothing or match the wrong thing. The count that matters (9 of 15) is in the note. notes: A HEALING escort op, not a fight -- nothing here is killed, and a verb scan would have made steps out of the healer AI. Of ten bullets only six are things the player does. Bullet [5] (the four conversation options) and bullet [6] (how the healer AI behaves, including that they wander off and that forcing them to rest gains nothing) are commentary. Bullet [8] is the completion THRESHOLD and an appraisal tier, not an action, so it rides in the objective step's note. Bullet [4]'s sub-bullet is the actual instruction -- talk to the two Pupil Palliators to make them follow -- so the two of them are one unordered group and both draw at once; a strict ladder would mark Palliator I and nothing else. ERA: the page writes the destination as 'East Ronfaure', bare, in both the Description and bullet [2], and it is not even a wiki link there. Campaign runs in the past era, so the live zone is almost certainly East Ronfaure (S) (zone 81) and not the present-day East Ronfaure (zone 101) that the written name resolves to. The page's own word is recorded because inventing the (S) would be inventing a name, and era_suffix_missing is flagged so a human can settle it. Everbloom Hollow needs no suffix. The injured NPCs are the objective and the page names almost none of them, so that step has no target and the counts live in its note. The header's Campaign Rank is a Bronze Ribbon of Service tier -- a CAMPAIGN rank, which has no schema field and is not a character level, so it is recorded here and flagged instead of being forced into gates.level. Bullet [8] also notes the healers have the MP for 4 of 5 without resting but not all 5. gates.repeatable and gates.expansion are left null: the Campaign Header carries no Repeatable and no Expansion field, and an explicit null is the tri-state 'the page did not say' rather than a claim that it does not repeat.

notes: This page is a stub and the honest answer is a two-rung ladder that stops in mid-air. The walkthrough has exactly two bullets: talk to Rasdinice, and travel to Castle Zvahl Baileys (S) or Castle Zvahl Keep (S). No hand-in step is invented for it, even though every other Intel gathering op in this batch ends by returning to the giver; guessing that rung is exactly the pattern-matching this rebuild exists to avoid. The 'After the walkthrough: Notes' bullet ('There seems to be no time limit') is an observation, not a step. notes: A timed chocobo delivery, and the shape that matters is that the DESTINATION is a choice of four. Bullet [1] is two steps: talk to the op's giver (the bullet calls him only 'the Campaign Ops NPC'; bullet [3] names him Emhi Tchaoryo), then talk to Yasmina, who asks which stronghold you will ride to. Bullet [1]'s sub-bullets are that menu of four with their measured times -- a list of candidates, not steps, and not an order to visit all four. So the ride step carries no zone: recording one of the four would put the marker in a place three players out of four cannot use. Bullet [2] is the delivery. There is nothing to click -- arriving at the Campaign Arbiter dismounts you and starts a cutscene by itself -- so it is a travel step whose target is the Arbiter. Yasmina's zone is not stated in the bullet, only her (G-5); BG Wiki's Yasmina page (REST API) gives Windurst Waters (S) (G-5), Chocobo NPC, which matches the op's own zone, so it is recorded and the lookup is named here. The op is timed and the target time depends on which stronghold you pick, which no packet reports -- time_gated. Times to beat, from bullet [1]: West Sarutabaruta (S) between 1:09 and 1:41, Fort Karugo-Narugo (S) 5:02 fast enough and 5:05 too slow, Meriphataud Mountains (S) 8:14 fast enough and 8:31 not, Sauromugue Champaign (S) 10:27 fast enough and 13:41 not. The 'After the walkthrough: Notes' bullet -- Northern Front strongholds do not contribute -- is a constraint on the choice, carried in the ride step's note. The header's Campaign Rank is a Brass Ribbon of Service tier -- a campaign rank, which has no schema field and is not a character level, so it is noted and flagged rather than written into gates.level. gates.repeatable and gates.expansion are left null: the Campaign Header carries no Repeatable and no Expansion field, and an explicit null is the tri-state 'the page did not say' rather than a claim that it does not repeat.

ride to whichever stronghold you chose -- West Sarutabaruta (S), Fort Karugo-Narugo (S), Meriphataud Mountains (S) or Sauromugue Champaign (S) -- so no zone is recorded. The Fort Karugo-Narugo option is the odd one: you must ride through Fivespires to Lamurara, C.C., entering by the small brick doors (the Phosphorous Ward will not open while mounted), and dismounting before that cutscene fires FAILS the op. Northern Front strongholds do not count.

Bullet [1]'s sub-bullets are that menu of four with their measured times -- a list of candidates, not steps, and not an order to visit all four. So the ride step carries no zone: recording one of the four would put the marker in a place three players out of four cannot use. Bullet [2] is the delivery. There is nothing to click -- arriving at the Campaign Arbiter dismounts you and starts a cutscene by itself -- so it is a travel step whose target is the Arbiter. Yasmina's zone is not stated in the bullet, only her (G-5); BG Wiki's Yasmina page (REST API) gives Windurst Waters (S) (G-5), Chocobo NPC, which matches the op's own zone, so it is recorded and the lookup is named here. The op is timed and the target time depends on which stronghold you pick, which no packet reports -- time_gated. Times to beat, from bullet [1]: West Sarutabaruta (S) 1:09 fast enough and 1:20 not, Fort Karugo-Narugo (S) 4:10 fast enough and 4:14 not, Meriphataud Mountains (S) 7:36, Sauromugue Champaign (S) 10:01 fast enough and 10:23 not. This page's Sauromugue Champaign sub-bullets are a turn-by-turn riding route through Fort Karugo-Narugo (S) and Meriphataud Mountains (S); it is route advice for one of the four choices, not a sequence of steps, and the zones it names are waypoints rather than destinations. The Notes bullet again says only that this tier wants faster times, not that the previous tier gates it. The header's Campaign Rank is an Iron Emblem of Service tier -- a campaign rank, noted and flagged, never gates.level. gates.repeatable and gates.expansion are left null: the Campaign Header carries no Repeatable and no Expansion field, and an explicit null is the tri-state 'the page did not say' rather than a claim that it does not repeat.

she gives the details and asks which stronghold you want to ride to. The bullet gives (G-5) but no zone; BG Wiki's Yasmina page puts her in Windurst Waters (S) at G-5 as the Chocobo NPC.

ride to whichever stronghold you chose -- West Sarutabaruta (S), Fort Karugo-Narugo (S), Meriphataud Mountains (S) or Sauromugue Champaign (S) -- so no zone is recorded. Arrival at the Campaign Arbiter dismounts you and starts a cutscene; nothing is clicked. The Fort Karugo-Narugo option is the odd one: you must ride through Fivespires to Lamurara, C.C., entering by the small brick doors (the Phosphorous Ward will not open while mounted), and dismounting before that cutscene fires FAILS the op. Northern Front strongholds do not count.
